# hackbuild-agents

> hackbuild-agents is a set of ESM packages under @hackbuild for simulated animals and the people round them in a browser sim: perception (saliency, odour, hearing, eye renders to an occupancy grid) and drives, choice, cue learning and sleep, each on a Rust core in wasm; a capsule mover with steering and a grid path planner; gameplay cameras that drive a three camera without importing three; a parameter registry for A/B work; views of the brain on the hackbuild-ui class layer; and a lockstep scenario runner for headless Chrome. No package loads a model, asset or weight file; randomness is injected as a seeded function.

Every package is ESM only with types included, installs from npm under @hackbuild, and is MIT. Each llms.md below lists the package's exports with signatures, minimal examples and the mistakes to avoid. Code: https://github.com/hackbuild/hackbuild-agents

## Packages

- [@hackbuild/agents-views](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/agents-views/llms.md): The brain bars, the associations table and the eye card of a simulated animal, as views you mount on any page with the hackbuild-ui look.
- [@hackbuild/cameras](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/cameras/llms.md): Gameplay cameras for a browser sim: follow, group framing, orbit, first person and split views, with shared damping, seeded shake and occlusion pull in.
- [@hackbuild/drives](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/drives/llms.md): Drives, choice with a reason, cue learning, sleep and a memory stream for simulated animals, on a Rust core in wasm.
- [@hackbuild/mover](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/mover/llms.md): A kinematic capsule mover and steering for agents that share space, with a grid path planner over the world colliders.
- [@hackbuild/scenario](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/scenario/llms.md): Run a built browser sim in the system Chrome in whole fixed steps, record or compare its trace against a golden file, and report motion checks with their legal ranges.
- [@hackbuild/senses](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/senses/llms.md): Perception for simulated animals: saliency, looming, an odour plume and scent tracking, hearing error, field of view vision and an occupancy grid from eye depth, on a Rust core in wasm.
- [@hackbuild/tunables](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/tunables/llms.md): A parameter registry with layer switches, presets and URL hash sharing for A/B work on agent behaviour.

## Quick starts

- [agents-views quick start](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/agents-views/quick.ts): the smallest program for @hackbuild/agents-views, typechecked in CI
- [cameras quick start](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/cameras/quick.ts): the smallest program for @hackbuild/cameras, typechecked in CI
- [drives quick start](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/drives/quick.ts): the smallest program for @hackbuild/drives, typechecked in CI
- [mover quick start](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/mover/quick.ts): the smallest program for @hackbuild/mover, typechecked in CI
- [scenario quick start](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/scenario/quick.ts): the smallest program for @hackbuild/scenario, typechecked in CI
- [senses quick start](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/senses/quick.ts): the smallest program for @hackbuild/senses, typechecked in CI
- [tunables quick start](https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/tunables/quick.ts): the smallest program for @hackbuild/tunables, typechecked in CI

# @hackbuild/agents-views

> The brain bars, the associations table and the eye card of a simulated animal, as views you mount on any page with the hackbuild-ui look.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-agents. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/agents-views/

## Purpose

- Draws what the animal is doing and why, what each act is worth now with the chosen one in pink, and how much it needs each thing.
- Draws what it has learned: cues by acts, each cell the net strength from 0 to 99, with how much it still pays attention to each cue.
- Makes an element the eye card: a canvas drawn from inside the animal's own eye, a switch for whose eyes, and a mode line.
- Mounts Yard, the dog simulator's whole stage and rack, from `@hackbuild/agents-views/yard`: the dog and his person in a 3D yard, the care verbs, the eye inset, the seven tabs with the drives bars and the associations table, the tune rack, the cortex model select and the setup panel.
- Ships each small view three ways that draw the same markup: a plain function over a host element, a custom element and a Vue component.
- Reads @hackbuild/drives and @hackbuild/cameras objects by their shape, so it has no runtime dependency on either.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/agents-views @hackbuild/drives @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui
```

`@virgilvox/hackbuild-ui` (0.10 or 0.11) is a peer: the views write its classes and never style themselves, so load its `hackbuild.css` on the page. `vue` (3.5 or later) is an optional peer, needed only for the `@hackbuild/agents-views/vue` entry. @hackbuild/drives is what the quick start feeds the views; @hackbuild/cameras gives the eye card its `FirstPerson` eye. Neither is a dependency of this package.

The `@hackbuild/agents-views/yard` entry needs `three` (0.186 or 0.187, its WebGPU build) and @hackbuild/motion-net, gait, tunables, senses, drives, cameras and weights, all optional peers so the small views install without them. The host passes the physics core (`@dimforge/rapier3d-compat`) and the models.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/agents-views

```ts
const ASSOCIATIONS_NOTE: "rows are cues, columns are acts. cells show net strength, excitation minus a separate inhibition that fades faster, so an extinguished cue partly comes back after a break. the attn column is each cue's associability: it rises after surprises and falls as the outcome becomes predictable. credit fades with delay, so a slow treat can reward whatever it is doing when it lands. if nothing is strong it offers tricks it was rewarded for before; teach a new word by praising whatever it does."
```

The explanation under the table: how net strength, attention and delayed credit work.

```ts
  reseed?: (params: string) => void;
  setup?: boolean;
  suiteUrl?: string;

}
```

Options of `mountYard`.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { associationsState, associationsTable, drivesBars, drivesBarsState } from "@hackbuild/agents-views";
import { Chooser, CueLearner, Drives, load, seededRng } from "@hackbuild/drives";

// the brain: two drives, three acts and a learner, all seeded
await load();
const rng = seededRng(7);
const drives = new Drives({ hunger: 1, play: 0.8 });
const chooser = new Chooser({ rng, options: ["idle", "eat", "fetch"] as const });
const learner = new CueLearner({ rng, actions: ["sit", "paw"] as const });

// the views: mount once, update each tick
const bars = drivesBars(document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div")));
const table = associationsTable(document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div")), { onReset: () => location.reload() });
let now = 0;
setInterval(() => {
  now += 0.5;
  drives.grow(0.5, { hunger: 0.02, play: 0.03 });
  const d = chooser.update(now, { idle: 0.1, eat: drives.rewardOf({ hunger: -0.5 }), fetch: drives.rewardOf({ play: -0.4 }) });
  bars.update(drivesBarsState(d, drives, { now }));
  table.update(associationsState(learner));
}, 500);
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { drivesBars } from "@hackbuild/agents-views";

const bars = drivesBars(document.querySelector("#brain") as HTMLElement);
bars.update({ behavior: "fetch", why: "play is high", utilities: { idle: 0.1, fetch: 0.6 }, drives: { play: 0.8, hunger: 0.3 } });
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import * as RAPIER from "@dimforge/rapier3d-compat";
import { mountYard } from "@hackbuild/agents-views/yard";

const yard = await mountYard(document.querySelector("#yard") as HTMLElement, {
  physics: async () => RAPIER,
  dog: "assets/dog.glb",
  human: "assets/human.glb",
  anims: "assets/anims.json",
  bar: document.querySelector("header"),
});
await yard.ready;
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Load the hackbuild-ui stylesheet (`hackbuild.css` from @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui) on the page. The views write its classes only and carry no styles, so without it the bars and the table draw as plain text.
- Mount a view once and call `update(state)` each tick. Calling `drivesBars(host)` again every frame rebuilds the panels and loses the in place bar motion.
- Call `load()` from @hackbuild/drives before making the `Chooser`, `Drives` or `CueLearner` you pass to `drivesBarsState` or `associationsState`; this package reads them by shape and never loads the wasm itself.
- Call the eye card's `frame()` from your render loop. `eyeInset` draws nothing by itself, and `draw` runs inside `who.eye.render`, so do not hide or restore the head yourself.
- Import Vue components from `@hackbuild/agents-views/vue`, not the main entry, and install `vue` for it; the main entry has no Vue code.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/agents-views: eyeInset needs at least one who` (`eyeInset` got an empty `who` list): pass at least one who entry

---

# @hackbuild/cameras

> Gameplay cameras for a browser sim: follow, group framing, orbit, first person and split views, with shared damping, seeded shake and occlusion pull in.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-agents. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/cameras/

## Purpose

- Follows a moving target from behind its heading, and pulls in at once when your raycast says something blocks the view.
- Frames a group of points so every one stays on screen at a fixed pitch and yaw.
- Orbits, zooms and pans from deltas, so input binding stays with your app.
- Puts an eye on an agent's head and hides that head for its own render only.
- Shakes with seeded value noise and decaying trauma, and splits the screen into one to four views.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/cameras three
```

The package imports nothing at run time. It writes `position.set`, `lookAt`, `fov` and `aspect` on the camera you pass, so a three `PerspectiveCamera` fits; three (`>=0.186.1 <0.188.0`) is a peer only for its types and for your scene. The quick start below uses three for the camera.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/cameras

```ts
interface CameraLike {
  aspect: number;
  fov: number;
  position: { x: number; y: number; z: number; set(x: number, y: number, z: number): unknown };
  lookAt(x: number, y: number, z: number): void;
}
```

The camera surface the rigs write: a three PerspectiveCamera fits, nothing is imported.

```ts
function damp(from: number, to: number, rate: number, dt: number): number
```

Frame rate independent exponential damping toward `to` at `rate` per second.

```ts
class FirstPerson {
  constructor(camera: CameraLike, head?: Scalable | null, forward?: number, up?: number);
  readonly camera: CameraLike;
  readonly forward: number;
  readonly head: Scalable | null;
  readonly up: number;
  place(head: V3, yaw: number, pitch: number): void;
  render(draw: () => void): void;
}
```

A first person eye on an agent's head.

```ts
class Follow {
  constructor(camera: CameraLike, o?: FollowOptions);
  readonly camera: CameraLike;
  dist: number;
  readonly o: Required<Omit<FollowOptions, "clear">> & Pick<FollowOptions, "clear">;
  update(p: V3, heading: number, dt: number, snap?: boolean): void;
}
```

Third person follow behind a moving target, pulled in when something blocks the view.

```ts
interface FollowOptions {
  backoff?: number;
  clear?: (from: V3, dir: V3, max: number) => number;
  distance?: number;
  lookHeight?: number;
  minDistance?: number;
  pitch?: number;
  smoothing?: number;
  yawSmoothing?: number;
}
```

Options of Follow; every field has a default.

```ts

  constructor(camera: CameraLike, o?: GroupOptions);
  readonly camera: CameraLike;
  dist: number;
  readonly o: Required<GroupOptions>;
  target: V3;
  solve(points: readonly V3[]): { dist: number; target: V3 };

```

Keeps every point in view: the crownfall shared camera.

```ts
interface GroupOptions {
  band?: number;

  centerPull?: number;
  maxDistance?: number;
  minDistance?: number;
  pad?: number;
  pitch?: number;
  yaw?: number;
}
```

Options of Group; every field has a default.

```ts
class Orbit {
  constructor(camera: CameraLike, yaw?: number, pitch?: number, dist?: number, target?: V3, limits?: { maxDist: number; maxPitch: number; minDist: number; minPitch: number });
  readonly camera: CameraLike;
  dist: number;
  readonly limits: { maxDist: number; maxPitch: number; minDist: number; minPitch: number };
  pitch: number;
  target: V3;
  yaw: number;

```

A free orbit camera driven by deltas (drag, wheel, keys); input binding stays with the app.

```ts
function orbitPosition(target: V3, yaw: number, pitch: number, dist: number): V3
```

Places a camera on an orbit around a target: yaw 0 behind +Z, pitch up from the ground.

```ts
type Rng = () => number
```

Uniform numbers in [0, 1), injected so a seed replays the same shake.

```ts
interface Scalable {
  scale: { x: number; y: number; z: number; set(x: number, y: number, z: number): unknown };
}
```

An object with a scale, such as a three Object3D head bone.

```ts
class Shake {
  constructor(rng: Rng, frequency?: number, decay?: number);
  readonly decay: number;
  readonly frequency: number;
  readonly amplitude: number;
  kick(amplitude: number, max?: number): void;
  step(dt: number): V3;
}
```

Shake: seeded value noise on three axes, amplitude decaying at `decay` per second.

```ts
function splitViewports(n: number, width: number, height: number): { h: number; w: number; x: number; y: number; yGl: number }[]
```

Viewports for 1 to 4 split views in pixels, top left origin; three wants bottom left, so `y` is flipped for it.

```ts
interface V3 {
  x: number;
  y: number;
  z: number;
}
```

A point or offset in metres, y up.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { Follow, Shake } from "@hackbuild/cameras";
import { PerspectiveCamera } from "three";

const camera = new PerspectiveCamera(50, 16 / 9, 0.1, 200);
// your raycast: here a wall 2 m behind the look target, along -z
const clear = (from: { z: number }, dir: { z: number }, max: number) => (dir.z < 0 ? Math.min(max, 2 / -dir.z) : max);
const follow = new Follow(camera, { distance: 4, clear });

// shake takes a seeded stream of its own, never the sim's
let seed = 7;
const shake = new Shake(() => ((seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647) / 2147483647));
shake.kick(0.4);

const dog = { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0, yaw: 0 };
for (let frame = 0; frame < 60; frame++) {
  dog.z += 0.02;
  follow.update(dog, dog.yaw, 1 / 60);
  camera.position.add(shake.step(1 / 60));
}
console.log(camera.position.toArray(), follow.dist);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Importing three inside code that uses this package only for the rigs: the rigs take any `CameraLike` (`position.set`, `lookAt`, `fov`, `aspect`), so a test or a non three renderer passes a plain object.
- Giving `Shake` the sim's rng: it draws only while shaking and per frame, so a shared stream ties the sim to the frame rate and breaks seeded replays. Give it a stream of its own, and never `Math.random`.
- Passing `snap = true` to `Follow.update` or `Group.update` every frame: it skips the damping. Snap on the first frame or after a teleport only.
- Hiding the head with `visible = false` for a first person view: that hides the whole subtree, body included. Use `FirstPerson.render(draw)`, which scales the head to 0.001 for that draw only.
- Passing `y` from `splitViewports` to three's `setViewport`: three counts from the bottom, so use `yGl`.

---

# @hackbuild/drives

> Drives, choice with a reason, cue learning, sleep and a memory stream for simulated animals, on a Rust core in wasm.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-agents. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/drives/

## Purpose

- Scores each act by how much it would reduce the animal's needs (drive reduction reward over named deficits).
- Picks an act by softmax with a commitment bonus, switches after a short latency for options that cannot wait, and returns a why sentence with every decision.
- Learns which cue goes with which act, with associability, eligibility traces, inhibition that fades and everyday non compliance; the state saves to JSON.
- Runs sleep pressure, a body clock and a sleep stage machine with a hypnogram, and ranks memories by recency, importance and relevance.
- Gates task layers and schedules heavy model calls so they start only when idle and inside a frame budget.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/drives
```

No peers and no dependencies. The wasm core ships inlined as base64, and `load()` with no argument decodes it, so it works from file:// with no fetch. The raw wasm is also exported as `@hackbuild/drives/wasm` if you would rather fetch it.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/drives

```ts
function bodyClock(hour: number): number
```

Sleepiness from the body clock at an hour 0 to 24 (peaks of activity near 7 and 19).

```ts
function bodyClockJs(hour: number): number
```

Sleepiness from the body clock at an hour 0 to 24, with Math.exp (see the wasm `bodyClock`).

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { Chooser, Drives, load, seededRng } from "@hackbuild/drives";

// the wasm core is inlined; load it once before any class
await load();
const drives = new Drives({ hunger: 1, fatigue: 1, play: 0.8 });
const chooser = new Chooser({ rng: seededRng(42), options: ["idle", "eat", "fetch", "rest"] as const });

// a minute of a sim at 10 Hz: needs grow, each act is scored by how much it would reduce them
for (let t = 0; t <= 60; t += 0.1) {
  drives.grow(0.1, { hunger: 0.02, fatigue: 0.01, play: 0.03 });
  const d = chooser.update(t, {
    idle: 0.05,
    eat: drives.rewardOf({ hunger: -0.5 }),
    fetch: drives.rewardOf({ play: -0.4, fatigue: 0.05 }),
    rest: drives.rewardOf({ fatigue: -0.25 }),
  });
  if (d.switched) console.log(t.toFixed(1), d.current, d.why);
}
```

### from the concepts

```ts
const d = chooser.update(now, utilities, ["fetch"]);
if (d.pending) lookAt(d.pending.id);
if (d.switched) log(d.why);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Await `load()` before constructing `Drives`, `Chooser`, `CueLearner`, `Sleep` or `MemoryStream` or calling `bodyClock`; each throws `wasm not loaded. call load() first.` otherwise. `bodyClockJs`, `seededRng`, `GoalBoost`, `Completion`, `LayerGate`, `InferenceScheduler` and `settled` are plain TypeScript and need no load.
- Pass an `Rng` (`seededRng(seed)` or your own `() => number`) to every class that takes `rng`; never `Math.random`. The class seeds its wasm stream from one draw of it, so the same seed replays the same choices.
- Option and action names are fixed at construction: `update`, `set`, `markDone` and `respond` throw on a name that was not in `options` or `actions`. Utilities you leave out score 0, and negative or non finite ones are clamped to 0.
- Call `chooser.markDone()` when the executor finishes the act. Without it the chooser treats the act as still running: it keeps the commitment bonus and samples again only when the dwell runs out.
- Call `free()` on wasm backed objects you drop in a long running page; the memory lives in the wasm heap until then.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/drives: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (a class or `bodyClock` was used before the core loaded): `await load()` once at start
- `@hackbuild/drives: start option <id> is not in the list` (`ChooserOptions.start` is not one of `options`): pass one of the option names
- `@hackbuild/drives: no option named <id>` (`set`, `update` reactive or forced named an unknown option): use the names given to the chooser
- `@hackbuild/drives: no action named <id>` (a learner call named an unknown action): use the names given to the learner
- `@hackbuild/drives: learner state version <n> is not 1` (`CueLearner.load` got a state of another version): save the state again with `toJSON()`

---

# @hackbuild/mover

> A kinematic capsule mover and steering for agents that share space, with a grid path planner over the world colliders.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-agents. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/mover/

## Purpose

- Moves capsules against axis aligned boxes and vertical cylinders, with step up, ceilings, wall sliding, substeps by distance and moving platform carry.
- Steers each agent among the others: a passing side per neighbour held for at least a second, so two agents head on each keep right instead of turning away and standing still.
- Keeps contact as a constraint, yields on a timer with a cool down, and inserts a side waypoint when an agent stalls.
- Plans a path round walls with A* on a grid over the colliders, pulled straight, for the steerer to walk.
- Draws no random numbers: the same inputs give the same steps.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/mover
```

No dependencies and no peers. It works on plain numbers, so a three scene, another renderer or none at all fits. `dist/mover.iife.js` is the single file build, a classic script that defines `HackbuildMover` for pages opened from file://.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/mover


```ts
function wallCyl(x: number, z: number, r: number, y0: number, y1?: number): CylCollider
```

A cylinder from `y0` to `y1` that only pushes sideways and is never stood on.

```ts
class World {
  constructor(colliders: Collider[], o?: WorldOptions);
  colliders: Collider[];
  readonly maxSubsteps: number;
  readonly stepUp: number;
  readonly substepLength: number;
  endFrame(): void;
  ground(x: number, z: number, maxY?: number, r?: number): { c: Collider; y: number } | null;
  step(a: Actor, dt: number): void;
}
```

Moves capsule actors against box and cylinder colliders with step up, ceilings, wall sliding and platform carry.

```ts
interface WorldOptions {
  maxSubsteps?: number;
  stepUp?: number;
  substepLength?: number;
}
```

Step height and substep limits of a `World`.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { type Actor, Steerer, World, box } from "@hackbuild/mover";

// two walkers head on in a 20 m yard; each keeps right and both arrive
const world = new World([box(0, 0, 0, 20, 20)]);
const walkers = [-4, 4].map((z, i) => {
  const steer = new Steerer(`w${i}`);
  steer.setGoal(0, -z);
  const body: Actor = { pos: { x: 0, y: 0, z }, vel: { x: 0, y: 0, z: 0 }, radius: 0.3, height: 1.7, grounded: true };
  return { steer, body, state: { id: `w${i}`, x: 0, z, vx: 0, vz: 0, radius: 0.3 } };
});
for (let t = 0, dt = 1 / 60; t < 12; t += dt) {
  const states = walkers.map((w) => w.state);
  for (const { steer, body, state } of walkers) {
    const out = steer.update(t, state, states);
    Object.assign(body.vel, { x: out.vx, z: out.vz });
    world.step(body, dt);
    Object.assign(state, { x: body.pos.x, z: body.pos.z, vx: out.vx, vz: out.vz });
  }
}
console.log(walkers.map((w) => `${w.state.id} at ${w.state.x.toFixed(2)}, ${w.state.z.toFixed(2)}`).join("; "));
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { planPath, Steerer, World, box, wallBox } from "@hackbuild/mover";

const world = new World([box(0, 0, 0, 12, 12), wallBox(0, 0, 6, 0.2, 0, 2)]);
const p = planPath(world, { x: 0, z: -2 }, { x: 0, z: 2 }, { radius: 0.3, cell: 0.2 });
const steer = new Steerer("walker");
if (p.ok) steer.setPath(p.waypoints);
else console.log(p.reason, p.why); // "goal-blocked", "no-way" or "too-large"
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- The steerer does not move anything. Apply `out.vx` and `out.vz` to your body (a `World` actor or your own), then write the new position and velocity back into the `AgentState` it reads next step; a state left stale makes every neighbour test wrong.
- Pass the same `now` clock in seconds to every steerer and the full list of agent states, the agent itself included. Hold sides, yields and the stall window all run on that clock.
- With moving platforms, call `moveCollider` before stepping and `world.endFrame()` once after every actor has stepped; skipping `endFrame` carries actors again next frame.
- The steerer alone does not get round a wall across the line to the goal. Call `planPath` and hand its waypoints to `setPath`, and plan again after colliders move; check `ok` and `reason` before using the waypoints.
- A goal inside a grown collider gives `goal-blocked`, and a gap within one cell of `2 * (radius + margin)` may read as shut; use a smaller `cell` instead of shrinking the radius.

## Errors this package throws

- `planPath` result `reason: "goal-blocked"` (the goal sits inside a grown collider): move the goal clear of colliders by the radius plus margin
- `planPath` result `reason: "no-way"` (no route on the grid, or a gap narrower than one cell over the pad): use a smaller `cell`, or open the gap
- `planPath` result `reason: "too-large"` (the grid would pass `maxCells`): pass tighter `bounds` or a larger `cell`
- `steerer.unreachable` is true (8 stalls on one goal): plan a path with `planPath`, or pick another goal
- an actor sinks or floats (no collider top under it, or `grounded` left false): put a floor `box` under the yard

---

# @hackbuild/scenario

> Run a built browser sim in the system Chrome in whole fixed steps, record or compare its trace against a golden file, and report motion checks with their legal ranges.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-agents. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/scenario/

## Purpose

- Opens a page in the installed Chrome through puppeteer-core and answers every network request from a pinned local file, or refuses it; page errors, console errors and blocked requests fail the run.
- Steps the sim in lockstep through `window.__sim`, fires actions at sim times or on page conditions, reads probes and takes screenshots.
- Records traces as golden files and compares later runs row by row, naming the first row that differs.
- Measures motion from a trace (jerk, sliding, state toggles, stalls, frame times) and reports each check with what was measured, the legal range and the fix.
- Runs the same lockstep core against a sim object inside a page, with no Node built ins and no puppeteer, through `@hackbuild/scenario/browser`.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/scenario puppeteer-core
```

`puppeteer-core` (25.18.1 up to 26) is a peer of the Node entry; no browser is downloaded. Chrome is found at `/Applications/Google Chrome.app` on macOS or `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, `google-chrome-stable`, `chromium` or `chromium-browser` on Linux, and `HB_CHROME` overrides the path. The `./browser`, `./profiler` and `./metrics` entries need neither puppeteer nor Chrome. The quick start uses Node built ins only besides the package.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { formatReport, reportPasses, runSuite, stallSeconds } from "@hackbuild/scenario";

// a page with the lockstep contract: window.__sim steps whole frames and returns a trace
const file = join(tmpdir(), "walker.html");
writeFileSync(file, `<script>let x = 0, v = 0; const rows = [];
window.__sim = { step(n) { for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { x += v / 60; rows.push([x, 0]); } }, trace: () => ({ rows }), go() { v = 1; } };</script>`);

// one seeded run of 4 sim seconds, offline, with a stall check on the trace
const report = await runSuite({
  file, mode: "check", offline: true,
  scenarios: [{
    name: "walks", seed: 1, seconds: 4, actions: [{ at: 0.5, js: "h.go()" }],
    checks: (t) => [{ what: "stall", unit: "s", measured: stallSeconds(t.rows as number[][], t.rows.map(() => true), 1 / 60), legal: { max: 1 }, constraint: "set by the walker" }],
  }],
});
console.log(formatReport(report));
process.exitCode = reportPasses(report) ? 0 : 1;
```

### from the concepts

```ts
import { checkMessage, sliding } from "@hackbuild/scenario/browser";

const xz = [[0, 0], [0, 0.02], [0.02, 0.04]];
const slide = sliding(xz, [0, 0, 1.2], 1 / 60);
console.log(checkMessage({ what: "slide share", measured: slide.share, legal: { max: 0.1 }, constraint: "set by the gait" }));
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Give the page `window.__sim` with `step(n)` and `trace()`, and stop its own animation loop when the hash starts with `#test`. A page that keeps its requestAnimationFrame loop running advances between chunks, and the trace differs on every run.
- Route every network request. A CDN import with no `npmCdn` or `pinned` route is blocked and fails the run; use `offline: true` only for a self contained build.
- Pass `goldenDir` with `mode: "record"` or `"compare"`; `runSuite` throws without it. Use `mode: "check"` to run checks with no goldens.
- Send page code as a string or as a function that closes over nothing. A function is sent by its source and runs in the page, where your Node variables do not exist.
- Import `@hackbuild/scenario/browser` in a page, never the main entry: the main entry imports puppeteer-core and Node built ins. Use `gpu: "default"` when you measure frame rate, since the default swiftshader flags may run almost no frames.

## Errors this package throws

- `no chrome found. set HB_CHROME to the browser binary.` (no Chrome at the known paths): install Chrome or set `HB_CHROME`
- `compare needs goldenDir: without it nothing is compared` (`runSuite` in compare mode with no `goldenDir`): pass `goldenDir`; `record needs goldenDir` is the same for record
- `runner: no window.__sim after 240 s` (the page never exposed its test API): check the page loads with `#test&seed=N`, or raise `readyMs`
- `route: pinned file missing: <file>` (a pinned route names a file that is not there): restore the file or fix the lock
- `route: pinned file does not match its sha256: <file>` (the local file changed): restore the pinned file or update the pin
- `route: route hit has neither file nor body` (a route returned a hit with no answer): return `file` or `body`
- `no raf sampler on the page. call installRafSampler before goto.` (`readRaf` on a page without the sampler): call `installRafSampler(page)` before navigation
- `scenario is not json: <reason>` (`parseScenario` got broken text): fix the JSON
- `<name>: seed must be a whole number` (a scenario seed with a fraction): use an integer seed
- `<name>: seconds must be above 0` (a scenario of no length): give it a positive length
- `<name>: check <what> needs legal with min or max` (a check spec with no legal range): add `legal`
- `trace needs rows, a list of lists` (`parseTrace` got another shape): pass a trace or golden file

---

# @hackbuild/senses

> Perception for simulated animals: saliency, looming, an odour plume and scent tracking, hearing error, field of view vision and an occupancy grid from eye depth, on a Rust core in wasm.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-agents. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/senses/

## Purpose

- Finds where the eye goes next: Itti Koch saliency on a rendered frame with top down bias, fixation dwell and inhibition of return that survives head turns.
- Smells: a puff plume in a meandering wind and a ground trail grid, two nostril sniffing in bouts, and a tracker that follows a trail, surges upwind and casts crosswind.
- Sees and remembers: field of view vision with range by size, motion and daylight, and remembered positions whose error grows with age.
- Hears with error: sound azimuth with front back confusion, and startles on looming objects.
- Maps: integrates eye depth into an occupancy grid with A* paths and frontiers; `/three` renders the eye's ID and depth buffers from a three scene.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/senses
```

The main entry has no dependencies and no peers; the wasm is inlined, so `await load()` needs no file. The `/three` entry (`Eye`, `cameraFromThree`) takes three (`>=0.186.1 <0.188.0`) as a peer: `npm install @hackbuild/senses three`.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { load, OdourField, Sniffer, Tracker, seededRng } from "@hackbuild/senses";

// the inlined wasm; load(url) or load(bytes) also work
await load();
const rng = seededRng(7);
// wind heading is measured from +x, so -pi/2 blows from the bowl toward the dog
const field = new OdourField({ rng, windHeading: -Math.PI / 2 });
const sniffer = new Sniffer({ rng });
const tracker = new Tracker({ rng });

const bowl = { id: 0, x: 0, z: 6, strength: 1 };
const dog = { x: 0, z: 0, heading: 0 };
let arrived = false;
for (let t = 0; t < 30; t += 1 / 30) {
  field.step(1 / 30, [bowl]);
  sniffer.tick(field, 1 / 30, t, true, { x: dog.x, z: dog.z + 0.3 }, { x: 0.03, z: 0 });
  const s = tracker.step(field, sniffer, 1 / 30, t, dog, dog.heading, arrived);
  // walk toward the waypoint at the speed the tracker asks for
  const to = s.waypoint ?? dog;
  const d = Math.hypot(to.x - dog.x, to.z - dog.z);
  arrived = d <= s.stopDist;
  if (!arrived) [dog.x, dog.z, dog.heading] = [dog.x + ((to.x - dog.x) / d) * s.speed / 30, dog.z + ((to.z - dog.z) / d) * s.speed / 30, Math.atan2(to.x - dog.x, to.z - dog.z)];
}
console.log(`dog at ${dog.x.toFixed(2)}, ${dog.z.toFixed(2)}; the bowl is at 0, 6`);
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Constructing a class before `await load()`: every class wraps a wasm object and throws `@hackbuild/senses: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` With no argument `load()` uses the inlined copy, so no wasm URL is needed.
- Passing `Math.random` as `rng`: each class seeds its wasm stream from one draw, so a seeded run replays only with `seededRng(seed)` or another seeded function.
- Importing three for the main entry: only `@hackbuild/senses/three` (`Eye`, `cameraFromThree`) needs three. Saliency and the grid take a 16 number camera array; build it with `cameraLook` when there is no three camera.
- Calling `Tracker.step` with `arrived` always false: the tracker keeps the same waypoint until you report arrival within `stopDist`.
- Loading `senses-three.iife.js` from file:// with no `window.THREE`: it reads three from the page, so set `window.THREE` from a module first.

## Errors this package throws

- `@hackbuild/senses: wasm not loaded. call load() first.` (a class or `cameraLook` ran before the wasm loaded): `await load()` once before constructing
- `saliency grid must be at least 8 by 8` (`Saliency` got `width` or `height` under 8): use a grid of 8 by 8 or more; the default is 80 by 40
- `frame is shorter than width * height * 4` (`Saliency.update` got a frame smaller than its size says): pass RGBA bytes of exactly width by height
- `camera needs 16 numbers: position, right, up, back, fov, aspect, near, far` (a camera array of the wrong length): build it with `cameraLook` or `cameraFromThree`
- `depth is shorter than width * height` (`OccupancyGrid.integrate` got a short depth buffer): pass the `depth` of an `EyePass` with its `depthWidth` and `depthHeight`

---

# @hackbuild/tunables

> A parameter registry with layer switches, presets and URL hash sharing for A/B work on agent behaviour.

Generated by tools/llms.mjs from the TypeDoc JSON, the README and the examples of hackbuild-agents. Human docs: https://hackbuild.github.io/hackbuild-agents/docs/tunables/

## Purpose

- Defines every number that shapes behaviour once, with its range, step, unit, note and where the default comes from.
- Gates whole features behind layer switches under one master switch, so each feature keeps a fallback you can compare live.
- Saves only the values that differ from their defaults, so new defaults reach old sessions, with explicit migrations between versions.
- Shares a setup as one `tune=` field in the URL hash, beside the other hash fields of your page.
- Builds a panel for the registry with DOM calls only, styled by the hackbuild-ui `hb-tunables` class.

## Install

```sh
npm install @hackbuild/tunables
```

No dependencies and no peers. The panel in `@hackbuild/tunables/dom` ships no styles: install @virgilvox/hackbuild-ui and load its hackbuild.css for the `hb-tunables` look. `dist/tunables.iife.js` is the single file build, a classic script that defines `HackbuildTunables` with the panel included, for pages opened from file://.

## Exports

### @hackbuild/tunables/dom

```ts
function bindPanel(host: HTMLElement, reg: Registry, opts?: PanelOptions): Panel
```

Builds a tune panel for a registry inside `host` with DOM calls only and keeps both in step.

```ts
interface Panel {
  root: HTMLElement;
  dispose(): void;
  refresh(): void;
}
```

A built panel: its root element, `refresh` to read the registry again and `dispose` to remove it.

```ts
interface PanelOptions {
  document?: Document;
  fileName?: string;
  groupLabels?: Record<string, string>;
  history?: { readonly state: unknown; replaceState(data: unknown, unused: string, url?: string): void };
  location?: { hash: string };
  onExport?: (json: string) => void;
  onImport?: (skipped: string[], error: Error | null) => void;
  open?: string[];
  prefix?: string;
  syncHash?: boolean;
}
```

Group labels, open groups, class prefix, hash sync and export and import hooks of a panel.

### @hackbuild/tunables

```ts
type ChangeListener = (key: string, value: number) => void
```

Called with the key and the new value after any change.

```ts
function createRegistry(opts?: RegistryOptions): Registry
```

Makes an empty registry; define parameters and layers on it, then `restore` and `fromUrlHash`.

```ts
function decimalsFor(step: number): number
```

Decimal places a value of this step shows: 0 for whole steps, else enough for the step.

```ts
function formatValue(def: ParamDef, v: number): string
```

A value as text with the decimal places its step calls for.

```ts
interface ParamDef {
  cite?: string;
  def: number;
  group: string;
  key: string;
  label: string;
  max: number;
  min: number;
  note?: string;
  source?: Source;
  step: number;
  unit?: string;
}
```

One tunable number: key, group, label, default, range, step, unit and where the default comes from.

```ts
interface Preset {
  label: string;
  values: Record<string, number>;
}
```

A named set of values that `applyPreset` writes in one go.

```ts
interface Registry {
  abPair(layer: string): { off: Record<string, number>; on: Record<string, number> };
  applyPreset(name: string): void;
  def(key: string): ParamDef;
  define(def: ParamDef): void;
  defineLayer(key: string, label: string, opts?: { def?: 0 | 1; group?: string; note?: string }): void;
  definePreset(name: string, preset: Preset): void;
  fromJSON(saved: unknown): string[];
  fromUrlHash(hash: string): string[];
  get(key: string): number;
  groups(): { group: string; keys: string[] }[];
  has(key: string): boolean;
  keys(): string[];
  layer(key: string): boolean;
  layers(): string[];
  load(values: Record<string, number>): string[];
  onChange(fn: ChangeListener): () => void;
  presets(): { label: string; name: string }[];
  reset(key?: string): void;
  restore(): string[];
  set(key: string, value: number): void;
  snapshot(): Record<string, number>;
  toJSON(): Saved;
  toUrlHash(): string;
}
```

The parameters, layers and presets of one app, with clamped set, saves, URL hash sharing and change events.

```ts
interface RegistryOptions {
  master?: string;
  migrate?: Record<number, (values: Record<string, number>) => Record<string, number>>;
  renames?: Record<string, string>;
  storage?: StorageLike;
  storageKey?: string;
  version?: number;
}
```

Master layer, storage, schema version, migrations and key renames of a registry.

```ts
interface Saved {
  d: Record<string, number>;
  ver: number;
}
```

Saved form: the schema version and only the values that differ from their defaults.

```ts
type Source = "measured" | "computed" | "vendor" | "inferred" | "unknown"
```

Where a default value comes from (RULES.md: every number says which).

```ts
interface StorageLike {
  getItem(key: string): string | null;
  setItem(key: string, value: string): void;
}
```

Minimal storage surface; `localStorage` fits, so does a Map wrapper in tests.

## Examples

### quick start

```ts
import { createRegistry } from "@hackbuild/tunables";
import { bindPanel } from "@hackbuild/tunables/dom";

// one master layer, one feature layer and one number with its range and source
const tune = createRegistry({ master: "L.organic", storage: localStorage, version: 1 });
tune.defineLayer("L.organic", "organic (off is the canned build)");
tune.defineLayer("L.plume", "sniffing in a turbulent plume");
tune.define({ key: "Se.fix", group: "senses", label: "fixation median", unit: "s", def: 0.83, min: 0.2, max: 2, step: 0.01, source: "measured" });
tune.restore();
tune.fromUrlHash(location.hash);

// a panel in a host with the hackbuild-ui hb-tunables class; the URL hash follows every change
const host = document.body.appendChild(document.createElement("div"));
host.className = "hb-tunables";
bindPanel(host, tune, { syncHash: true });

tune.onChange((key, value) => console.log(key, value, "layer on:", tune.layer("L.plume")));
tune.set("Se.fix", 5); // clamped to 2
```

## Mistakes to avoid

- Define every key before you `get`, `set`, apply a preset or read a hash: an unknown key throws `tunables: no parameter named <key>`. Call `restore()` and `fromUrlHash()` after the definitions, not before.
- `layer(key)` is false whenever the master layer is off, whatever the layer's own value. Name the master in `createRegistry` and define it with `defineLayer`.
- Never reuse a key with a new meaning: old saves and shared hashes would load the old number into it. Give the new meaning a new key and map the old one in `renames`, or drop it.
- Saves hold only values that differ from their defaults; do not snapshot every value into storage yourself, or new defaults never reach saved sessions. A save of another version needs a `migrate` entry or nothing is kept.
- The panel ships no styles. Put the `hb-tunables` class on the host and load the hackbuild-ui stylesheet; do not set `innerHTML` on labels, they are text by design.

## Errors this package throws

- `tunables: no parameter named <key>` (`get`, `set`, `def`, a preset or `abPair` named a key that was never defined): define it first, or check the key
- `tunables: <key> is defined twice` (`define` or `defineLayer` called twice with one key): define each key once
- `tunables: <key> default <def> is outside <min> to <max>` (the default is out of its range): fix the range or the default
- `tunables: <key> step must be above 0` (a step of 0 or less): pass a positive step
- `tunables: saved settings must be an object` (`fromJSON` got something other than an object): pass the parsed output of `toJSON`
- `tunables: no preset named <name>` (`applyPreset` with an unknown name): define it with `definePreset`
